item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Firstly: I read the rules of the contest and now realize the "lone survivor" thing was an option for the story. I guess that makes my complaints regarding it weaker. I am aware of it but, honestly, I don't want to edit the comment anymore so I am acknowledging it here.

The premise is all right and the action parts were written well enough to be enjoyable to go through, but the punchline fell flat.

It's one thing to have this MTF "somewhere" because of "some reason" dealing with murder-candy-pumpkins and it is funny because "it is Halloween, you see?"

Now when the leader HAS to end the threath to the cost of his own life, leaving the clueless rookie as the only survivor, and the lone survivor comes back to the site and the first one he sees asks "Hey! Where have you been while all of were having fun partying?! With candies!!" (*wink wink*, says the narrator) that's too much.

This kind of twist works because while the whole of the article might give the appearance of "childish" or "wacky" or whatever it may be going for, there is enough foreshadowing for the revelation to make sense in hindsight. Here, after the leader's sacrifice (where it starts to seem like things were, actually, supposed to be taken seriously) now I have to think:

  • "So those that turned into candy were actually dead dead?" (I was expecting them to come back somehow, in a "It was all an illusion!" thing after defeating the last enemy with came with an obvious subtext of "WARNING, BOSS, WARNING, BOSS" as the ground rumbled (more "Dumb fun story!" material, by the way), and
  • "So after that first encounter, they lowered their guard only what, 20 seconds?" (You don't survive to tell a rookie "You get used to it." if that's how you act in the field), and
  • "Why were the 4 of them out there alone whithout communication to any other site personnel?", and
  • "So no one knew they were out in a mission?" (The story sure didn't even hint that.)

And it all starts to sound too dumb to take seriously.

To be clear, I had no problem with all of these things up until the point the story asked me to buy it as "serious things happenned". In the end I felt no connection at all to the clichéd "rookie broken after first mission goes south" and overall it felt like a waste of my time to read an epileptic story which seems to want to be funny and wacky and then sad while also being funny.

It does seem, however, like the tale was good enough to be popular. My advice, if you write something similar next time, is that the tonal shift has to make at least a little of sense, otherwise, it can feel awful (it obviously did not for the majority of the commenters here, but I hope you see my point). I would recommend thinking of how everything would read in hindsight and maybe foreshadowing the twist a little if applicable (if done well, these feel nice for the reader to think about after being made aware of the revelation).

item.content:encoded:
I could get over the unprofessional and clueless MTF operatives if the banter was good enough, or if there was any hilarity to the scenario besides the end, but the dialogue and characters were as basic as Halo NPCs.

And while candy transfiguration is a pretty alright death, it's not nearly played up well enough to set up the punchline.

All in all, it's really not well-written in the slightest. Funny concept, sure. But the prose doesn't pull its weight in being either a playful, entertaining romp, or juxtaposing the sillyness of the situation vs the horror of Delta's experience. Everything is just belted out so very plainly. There's little to enjoy beyond the premise.
